- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.9) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., >85) by overshooting downward; cap forecast decline at 5–7% below peak.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast horizon); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for early days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., -1.98, -0.54, -0.52), model tends to lag in correction; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lagged sentiment trend.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture sharp downward turns after 10–15 days; apply a “sudden drop” heuristic: if true outcome drops >5% from prior day, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
